# 1. Host plant data

Curated dataset for host plant associations for Danainae butterflies including information for ATPa resistance form & cardenolide content.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)
library(ape)
library(phytools)
library(ggtree)
library(stringr)
library(ggtree)
library(treeio)
library(ggimage)
library(stringr)
library(ggnewscale)
```

```{r}
plant_butterfly_long_all = read.csv("./plant_butterfly_long_all.csv")
```

# 2. Danaini phylogeny

Phylogenetic tree for Danaiini butterflies prepared in this study

```{r}
# Read tree
tr_new = ape::read.tree("./Danaini_phylo_tree//Danaini_concat.treefile")

# Canonical name cleaner: underscores -> spaces, trim, collapse multiple spaces
clean_name = function(x){
  stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(as.character(x), "_", " "))
}

# Clean tree tips ONCE
tr_new$tip.label = clean_name(tr_new$tip.label)

# Outgroups (same cleaning)
outgroups = clean_name(c("Tellervo zoilus", "Mechanitis polymnia"))

# Host species (same cleaning)
host_species = plant_butterfly_long_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(butterfly_species),
                clean_name(butterfly_species) != "") %>%
  dplyr::pull(butterfly_species) %>%
  clean_name() %>%
  unique()

# Diagnostics (so you see problems immediately)
missing_outgroups = setdiff(outgroups, tr_new$tip.label)

# Prune and root
tips_keep = unique(c(intersect(tr_new$tip.label, host_species), outgroups))
tr_keep   = ape::keep.tip(tr_new, tips_keep)
tr_rooted = ape::root(tr_keep, outgroup = outgroups, resolve.root = TRUE)

# Plot
ggtree(tr_rooted, branch.length = "none", ladderize = FALSE) +
  geom_tiplab(size = 2)
```

Check which species are only present in tree or host plant data

# 3. Broad Danaini phylogeny (55 species)

## 3.1 Ancestral milkweed clade & Ascl use reconstruction

Using the plant_butterfly_long_all dataset, we generate host use data for the Asclepias genus and the milkweed clade (Asclepiadoideae and Secamonoideae subfamilies) using an "at least one" approach. The butterfly species is coded as using that plant if it has at least one plant genera from that plant group in its host list.

```{r}
#host plant use based on "at least one", with three options (nested states): none, milkweed clade, or asclepias

host_data_permissive_three <- plant_butterfly_long_all %>%
  group_by(butterfly_species) %>%
  summarize(
    # Check for AT LEAST ONE 'present' in each category
    has_asclepias      = any(plant_genus == "Asclepias" & present == 1),
    has_milkweed = any((plant_subfamily == "Asclepiadoideae" | plant_subfamily == "Secamonoideae") & present == 1)
  ) %>%
  mutate(host_use = case_when(
    # Priority 1: Any use of Asclepias
    has_asclepias ~ "asclepias",
    
    # Priority 2: Any use of Asclepiadoideae (excluding species already classified as Asclepias)
    has_milkweed ~ "milkweed",
    
    # Fallback
    TRUE ~ "none"
  )) 

# Check the counts for your new discrete states
table(host_data_permissive_three$host_use)
```

```{r}
clean_tip = function(x) str_squish(str_replace_all(as.character(x), "_", " "))

# import the tree we saved earlier
tree0 = read.tree("./danaini_species_final_tree.newick")
tree0$tip.label = clean_tip(tree0$tip.label)

# clean butterfly species names
host_data_permissive_three$butterfly_species <- trimws(host_data_permissive_three$butterfly_species)

# filter the dataframe to match the tree
final_host_data_cleaned <- host_data_permissive_three %>%
  filter(butterfly_species %in% tree0$tip.label)

# explicitly set the levels in order
final_host_data_cleaned$host_use <- factor(
  final_host_data_cleaned$host_use, 
  levels = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias")
)

# create the names vector 
host_states <- setNames(final_host_data_cleaned$host_use, 
                        final_host_data_cleaned$butterfly_species)

# verify that they're the same
length(setdiff(names(host_states), tree0$tip.label))
```

Next, we model the evolution of host-plant association as a discrete multi-state character trait with three levels: none (no milkweed association), milkweed (association with at least one genera in the Asclepiadoideae and Secamonoideae subfamilies), and Asclepias (association with the Asclepias genus). We perform ancestral state reconstruciton using a maximum likelihood Mk model, with transition states estimated under a symmetric model (assuming equal rates for gain and loss of specific host associations).

```{r}
# fit ASR
fit_plot <- fitMk(tree0, host_states, model = "ER")
anc_states_plot <- ancr(fit_plot)

# organize for plotting, take the Likelihoods (ace) and add the node numbers
asr_df <- as.data.frame(anc_states_plot$ace)
asr_df$node <- (length(tree0$tip.label) + 1):(length(tree0$tip.label) + tree0$Nnode)

# add combined probabilities for the milkweed clade and asclepias
asr_df= asr_df %>%
  mutate(
    milkweed_combined = milkweed + asclepias
  )
```

## 3.2 Plotting

We visualized the phylogenetic tree and associated data using the R package ggtree, employing a cladogram transformation to emphasize evolutionary transitions independently of absolute branch lengths. Host-plant associations were plotted as a multi-column heatmap using the gheatmap function, with distinct color scales for the milkweed clade and the genus Asclepias managed via the ggnewscale package. Finally, marginal ancestral state probabilities were overlaid onto internal nodes as pie charts using the nodepie and inset functions, providing a spatially integrated representation of host-use evolution and model uncertainty.

```{r}
full_palette <- c(
  "none"            = "grey90",       # Neutral grey for non-host plants
  "milkweed"        = "#d7c0dd",    # Light purple (Milkweed clade)
  "asclepias"       = "#65338f"    # Dark purple (Asclepias genus)
)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Fig 1: Danaini tree + ASR pies + host-use strip + ATPα strip
#   - Host strip: milkweed clade / Asclepias (0/1)
#   - ATPα strip: LAN/LSN/VSN/VSH/unknown
# ============================================================

abbr_tip = function(x){
  x = clean_tip(x)
  vapply(x, function(z){
    parts = strsplit(z, " ")[[1]]
    if (length(parts) >= 2 && nchar(parts[1]) > 0) paste0(substr(parts[1], 1, 1), ". ", parts[2]) else z
  }, character(1))
}

p = ggtree(tree0, branch.length = "none", ladderize = FALSE, size = 0.3, color = "grey40") 

tree_xmax = max(p$data$x, na.rm = TRUE)

p = p +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = abbr_tip(label)),
              offset = 1, size = 3, fontface = "italic",
              align = TRUE, linetype = 0) +
  # show node numbers
  # geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node), size=4, color="purple") +
xlim_tree(tree_xmax + 4)

# ============================================================
# ---- tribe and subtribe annotation ----
# ============================================================
tree0$node.label = NULL  # remove bootstrap labels

df_node_labels = tibble::tibble(
  node = c(
    # subtribes
    100, 85, 63, 60,

    # genera
    104, 101, 94, 91, 86, 68, 64,

    # Danaus subgenera
    109, 107, 106
  ),
  clade = c(
    # subtribes
    "Danaina", "Amaurina", "Euploeina", "Itunina",

    # genera
    "Danaus", "Tirumala", "Parantica", "Ideopsis", "Amauris", "Euploea", "Idea",

    # Danaus subgenera
    "Danaus", "Salatura", "Anosia"
  ),
  label_type = c(
    rep("subtribe", 4),
    rep("genus", 7),
    rep("subgenus", 3)
  )
)

p = p %<+% df_node_labels +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +

  # subtribes: strongest emphasis
  geom_label2(
    aes(subset = !isTip & !is.na(clade) & label_type == "subtribe", label = clade),
    size = 3.1,
    label.size = 0.22,
    label.padding = grid::unit(0.16, "lines"),
    fill = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    nudge_x = -0.85
  ) +

  # genera: medium emphasis
  geom_label2(
    aes(subset = !isTip & !is.na(clade) & label_type == "genus", label = clade),
    size = 3.1,
    label.size = 0.22,
    label.padding = grid::unit(0.16, "lines"),
    fill = "grey98",
    fontface = "plain",
    nudge_x = -0.85
  ) +

  # subgenera: lightest emphasis
  geom_label2(
    aes(subset = !isTip & !is.na(clade) & label_type == "subgenus", label = clade),
    size = 2.8,
    label.size = 0.20,
    label.padding = grid::unit(0.16, "lines"),
    fill = "grey98",
    fontface = "italic",
    nudge_x = -0.65
  )

p
```

```{r}
# ---- ATPα strip ----
atpa_mat = plant_butterfly_long_all %>%
  distinct(butterfly_species, atpa_state) %>%
  mutate(tip = clean_tip(butterfly_species),
         atpa_state = replace_na(atpa_state, "unknown")) %>%
  distinct(tip, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(tip, atpa_state) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("tip") %>%
  as.data.frame()

atpa_mat = atpa_mat[tree0$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]
atpa_mat$atpa_state[is.na(atpa_mat$atpa_state)] = "unknown"

p = gheatmap(p, atpa_mat, offset = 0.01, width = 0.02, colnames = FALSE, color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = expression("ATP"*alpha*" state"),
    values = c("VSH"="#ed1c2c","VSN"="#f36f21","LSN"="#fec12b","LAN"="#3a6a9e","unknown"="grey85"),
    breaks = c("VSH","VSN","LSN","LAN","unknown"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()

p
```

```{r}
# prepare the 3-column binary dataframe
host_strip <- final_host_data_cleaned %>%
  # select species of interest
  select(butterfly_species, has_asclepias, has_milkweed) %>%
  mutate(
    asclepias     = factor(ifelse(has_asclepias, "asclepias_1", "asclepias_0"), 
                           levels = c("asclepias_0", "asclepias_1")),
    milkweed      = factor(ifelse(!is.na(has_milkweed) & has_milkweed, "milkweed_1", "milkweed_0"), 
                    levels = c("milkweed_0", "milkweed_1"))
  ) %>%
  # gheatmap REQUIRES species names as rownames
  column_to_rownames("butterfly_species") %>%
  # select only the two columns for the strip
  select(milkweed, asclepias)

# ensure the order matches the tree tips exactly
host_strip <- host_strip[tree0$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]
```

```{r}
# host use binary visualization
col_milkweed     = "#d7c0dd" 
col_asclepias    = "#65338f"

p <- gheatmap(p, host_strip, 
              offset = 0.3, 
              width = 0.04, 
              colnames = FALSE, 
              color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Host use",
    values = c(
      "milkweed_0" = "grey95", "milkweed_1" = col_milkweed,
      "asclepias_0" = "grey95", "asclepias_1" = col_asclepias
    ),
    breaks = c("milkweed_1", "asclepias_1"),
    labels = c("Milkweed clade", "Asclepias"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  new_scale_fill()

print(p)
```

# 4. Focused subset (18 species)

## 4.1 Ancestral Ascl use reconstruction

Prepare focused subset with species that have ATPa sequence

```{r}
# species with known ATPα state
atpa_known_species = plant_butterfly_long_all %>%
  mutate(
    tip = clean_tip(butterfly_species),
    atpa_state = replace_na(atpa_state, "unknown")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(tip),
    tip != "",
    !is.na(atpa_state),
    atpa_state != "",
    atpa_state != "unknown"
  ) %>%
  distinct(tip, atpa_state)

# host-use data with clean names
host_focused = host_data_permissive_three %>%
  mutate(tip = clean_tip(butterfly_species)) %>%
  filter(tip %in% tree0$tip.label) %>%
  mutate(
    asclepias_use = ifelse(has_asclepias, "asclepias", "no_asclepias")
  ) %>%
  select(tip, asclepias_use)

# keep only species with BOTH ATPα state and host-use data
focused_species = intersect(atpa_known_species$tip, host_focused$tip)

length(focused_species)
focused_species
```

Prune tree and prepare Asclepias-use state vector

```{r}
# prune tree to focused species
tree_focused = keep.tip(tree0, focused_species)

# prepare Asclepias-use states for focused tree
asclepias_states_focused = host_focused %>%
  filter(tip %in% tree_focused$tip.label) %>%
  distinct(tip, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(tip, asclepias_use) %>%
  deframe()

# ensure order matches tree tips
asclepias_states_focused = asclepias_states_focused[tree_focused$tip.label]

asclepias_states_focused = factor(
  asclepias_states_focused,
  levels = c("no_asclepias", "asclepias")
)

# checks
table(asclepias_states_focused)
setdiff(tree_focused$tip.label, names(asclepias_states_focused))
any(is.na(asclepias_states_focused))
```

Save tree for hyphy

```{r}
write.tree(
  tree_focused,
  file = "./Hyphy_H1H2/danaini_focused_atpa_host_species.newick"
)
```

Ancestral Asclepias-use reconstruction

```{r}
# Fit binary ASR model for Asclepias use
fit_ascl_focused = fitMk(
  tree_focused,
  asclepias_states_focused,
  model = "ER"
)

# Estimate ancestral states
anc_ascl_focused = ancr(fit_ascl_focused)

# Extract node probabilities
ascl_asr_df = as.data.frame(anc_ascl_focused$ace)

# Add internal node numbers
ascl_asr_df$node = (length(tree_focused$tip.label) + 1):
  (length(tree_focused$tip.label) + tree_focused$Nnode)

# View ASR results
ascl_asr_df
```

## 4.2 Plotting

```{r}
# palettes
ascl_palette = c("no_asclepias" = "grey90", "asclepias" = "#65338f")
atpa_palette = c("VSH" = "#ed1c2c", "VSN" = "#f36f21", "LSN" = "#fec12b", "LAN" = "#3a6a9e")

# observed tip strips
atpa_strip_focused = atpa_known_species %>%
  filter(tip %in% tree_focused$tip.label) %>%
  distinct(tip, atpa_state) %>%
  mutate(atpa_state = factor(atpa_state, levels = c("VSH", "VSN", "LSN", "LAN"))) %>%
  select(tip, atpa_state) %>%
  column_to_rownames("tip") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  .[tree_focused$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]

host_strip_focused = host_focused_tree %>%
  mutate(asclepias_use = factor(asclepias_use, levels = c("no_asclepias", "asclepias"))) %>%
  select(tip, asclepias_use) %>%
  column_to_rownames("tip") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  .[tree_focused$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]

# keep only strongly supported nodes
ascl_asr_df_plot = ascl_asr_df %>%
  filter(no_asclepias > 0.75 | asclepias > 0.75)

# base tree
p_focused = ggtree(
  tree_focused,
  branch.length = "none",
  ladderize = FALSE,
  size = 0.3,
  color = "grey40"
)

tree_focused_xmax = max(p_focused$data$x, na.rm = TRUE)

p_focused = p_focused +
  geom_tiplab(
    aes(label = abbr_tip(label)),
    offset = 0.8,
    size = 3,
    fontface = "italic",
    align = TRUE,
    linetype = 0
  ) +
  xlim_tree(tree_focused_xmax + 3)

# ATPα strip first
p_focused = gheatmap(
  p_focused,
  atpa_strip_focused,
  offset = 0.01,
  width = 0.03,
  colnames = FALSE,
  color = NA
) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = expression("ATP"*alpha*" state"),
    values = atpa_palette,
    breaks = c("VSH", "VSN", "LSN", "LAN"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()

# Asclepias-use strip second
p_focused = gheatmap(
  p_focused,
  host_strip_focused,
  offset = 0.16,
  width = 0.03,
  colnames = FALSE,
  color = NA
) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Host use",
    values = ascl_palette,
    breaks = c("asclepias", "no_asclepias"),
    labels = c("Asclepias", "Non-Asclepias"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()

# ASR pies for strongly supported nodes only
pies_ascl = nodepie(
  ascl_asr_df_plot,
  cols = c("no_asclepias", "asclepias"),
  alpha = 1
)

pies_ascl = lapply(pies_ascl, function(g) {
  g +
    scale_fill_manual(values = ascl_palette) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
})

# final plot
p_focused_final = inset(
  p_focused,
  pies_ascl,
  width = 0.05,
  height = 0.05
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(-0.15, 1),
    legend.justification = c(0, 1),
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm")
  )

p_focused_final

ggsave("./Fig1_asr_focused.png", p_focused_final, width = 10, height = 10)
```
